(1) raw line 83, klaassen-definitive-guide: checked:2026-08-23, due:2027-02-23 = checked+6mo exactly; live-verified publication 2026-02-09 (WebFetch, byline Klaassen, quote confirmed verbatim) → correct pub+6mo = 2026-08-09, already 14 days in the PAST as of the citation's own checked date — this stamp was miscalculated as fresh on the day it was written. (2) raw line 84, klaassen-expanded-loop: checked:2026-07-31, due:2027-01-31 = checked+6mo; live-verified publication 29 May 2026 (WebFetch, byline Klaassen) → correct pub+6mo = 2026-11-29, two months tighter than stated. (3) raw line 85, klaassen-compound-run: checked:2026-07-30, due:2027-01-30 = checked+6mo; live-verified publication 11 Dec 2025 (WebFetch, bylines Shipper & Klaassen) → correct pub+6mo = 2026-06-11, already ~2.5 months in the past as of the citation's own checked date. All three URLs sampled alive (3/3) and byline-confirmed; only the due-date arithmetic is wrong, not the cited content.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Recompute all three `due` fields from each source's publication date (2026-02-09 / 2026-05-29 / 2025-12-11) per §11a, not from `checked`. If a citation is meant as durable/definitional rather than a currency claim, use `due:none` under the durable-account variant with explicit body-dating instead — after checking §2a's condition-2 opinion exclusion, which the newest addition (klaassen-definitive-guide) currently fails.
